$comment: MCP tool contract for hubmcp (backend/cmd/hubmcp). Frozen; edit only via a CCR to contract-steward. JSON Schemas are 2020-12. See README.md in this folder.

server.name: hubmcp
server.title: Integration Hub
server.description: Lets an AI assistant discover and call Integration Hub integrations as a tenant, and (optionally) read operational state as an admin viewer.

env.name: HUB_BASE_URL
env.description: Base URL of the Hub gateway, e.g. http://localhost:8080. The admin API is reached at HUB_ADMIN_BASE_URL or, if unset, HUB_BASE_URL with /admin/v1.

env.name: HUB_API_KEY
env.description: Tenant API key (scope `invoke`; add `dry_run` to enable hub_dry_run). Sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Never logged or echoed.

env.name: HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN
env.description: OIDC access token with role viewer (or tenant_viewer). When unset, the hub_admin_* tools are not registered at all.

env.name: HUB_ADMIN_BASE_URL
env.description: Override for the control-plane base URL, e.g. http://localhost:8081/admin/v1.

rules: Tenant tools (no `hub_admin_` prefix) MUST NOT reveal vendor names, account names, integration versions or transformer versions. The server strips the X-Hub-Integration-Version header and never puts it in tool output.
The only exception is hub_dry_run, which returns the upstream request shape (secrets redacted) by design. Its description says so.

hub_invoke MUST refuse (without calling the Hub) when the integration has moves_money_or_quota=true and the input lacks confirm=true or idempotency_key. The server checks the flag via getIntegration before every such invoke (cached ≤ 60 s).
Admin tools are read-only and never call mutating admin operations (no unseal, replay, purge, pause or force).
Errors from the Hub are returned as tool results with isError=true and the canonical error object, not as protocol errors.
A 202 is reported as outcome=queued, never as success.

tools.name: hub_list_integrations
tools.title: List integrations
tools.description: List the integrations this API key's tenant can invoke. Each item gives the integration_id (use it in other hub_* tools), its capability (the shape of the request body, e.g. events.track@v1), the operations it supports, its delivery mode (sync returns a result immediately; wait/async may return 'queued'), whether it is interactive, whether it is paused, and whether it moves money or quota (then hub_invoke needs confirm=true and an idempotency_key). Use this first when the user mentions a third-party action and you don't know the integration id.
safety: Read-only.
Output is the caller-facing IntegrationSummary only; no vendor/account/version fields exist in it.

tools.name: hub_describe_integration
tools.title: Describe an integration
tools.description: Get everything needed to call one integration correctly: its delivery policy (mode, wait window, TTL, what happens when the upstream is down) and, for each operation, the canonical request and response JSON Schemas. Always call this before hub_invoke or hub_dry_run so you build a body that matches request_schema exactly — unknown fields are rejected. Fields tagged x-pii hold personal data: only send values the user actually provided.

capability.description: hub-public CapabilityDescriptor (operations[].request_schema / response_schema are JSON Schema documents).

safety: Read-only.
Composes two caller-API reads; neither exposes vendor/account/version.

tools.name: hub_dry_run
tools.title: Dry-run an integration (developer tool)
tools.description: Show the exact upstream HTTP request the Hub WOULD send for a canonical body, without sending anything (no side effects, no quota used). Use it to check a body before a real call, or when the user is developing an integration. IMPORTANT: unlike every other tenant tool, the result reveals the upstream request shape (URL, headers, body) with secrets replaced by ***; do not present it to end users as the integration's contract, and never build logic on it — it changes whenever the Hub cuts over. Requires an API key with the dry_run scope; otherwise you get FORBIDDEN.

body.description: Canonical request body matching the operation's request_schema (see hub_describe_integration).

session.description: X-Hub-Session from step 1 of a multi-step flow.

safety: Documented exception to the no-vendor-leak rule (x-audience: integration-developers).
No upstream call, no queue entry, no idempotency record.
Secrets are redacted by the Hub; hubmcp additionally refuses to output any header value not equal to *** for headers listed in `redacted`.

tools.name: hub_invoke
tools.title: Invoke an integration
tools.description: Call an integration for real with a canonical body. This has real-world effects (events sent, messages delivered, money or quota possibly consumed). Steps: 1) hub_describe_integration to get the request_schema; 2) build the body; 3) call hub_invoke. Always pass an idempotency_key (a stable string per logical action, e.g. 'order-8821-created') so a retry cannot double-send. If the integration has moves_money_or_quota=true you MUST first show the user what will be sent and get explicit approval, then call with confirm=true. Results: outcome=completed gives the canonical result; outcome=queued means accepted but NOT done yet — tell the user and use hub_get_request with the request_id to follow up; outcome=error gives a canonical error (if retryable is true you may retry with the same idempotency_key after retry_after_ms). For multi-step operations, pass the session returned by step 1.

idempotency_key.description: Strongly recommended; mandatory when moves_money_or_quota is true.

prefer_async.description: Send Prefer: respond-async (accept a queued answer if the upstream is down).

session.description: X-Hub-Session for step 2+ of a multi-step flow.

confirm.description: Must be true for integrations with moves_money_or_quota=true, after the user explicitly approved this exact call.

error.description: Canonical error object (code, message, retryable, retry_after_ms, ...), or a local refusal with code CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED / IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED.

safety: Side-effecting. destructiveHint=true so clients prompt the user.

Pre-check: GET integration; if paused, return the error without invoking; if moves_money_or_quota and (confirm != true or no idempotency_key) return outcome=refused, code CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED or IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED, without calling the Hub.

Never forwards any header that could select a vendor/account/version (none exist in the contract; hubmcp sends only Authorization, Idempotency-Key, Prefer, X-Request-Deadline, X-Hub-Session, traceparent).
Strips X-Hub-Integration-Version and X-Hub-Served-By from output.
Never auto-retries a non-retryable error; retries a retryable one at most once and only when idempotency_key is set.

tools.name: hub_get_request
tools.title: Get request status
tools.description: Check the status of an earlier hub_invoke by request_id — use it after an outcome=queued. status is one of accepted, in_flight, retry_scheduled, parked (waiting for the upstream to recover), succeeded (result holds the canonical response), failed or dead_lettered (error holds why), expired (it was not delivered before its TTL). Do not poll in a tight loop: wait at least a few seconds between calls and tell the user it is still pending.
safety: Read-only.
Only the calling tenant's requests are visible (others give REQUEST_NOT_FOUND).

tools.name: hub_admin_search_requests
tools.title: Search requests (admin, read-only)
tools.description: Operator tool: search the Hub's request ledger across tenants (or within your tenant scope) by integration, status, error code, vendor, account and time range. Unlike tenant tools, results include vendor_id, account_id and integration version, because this is the control plane. Use it to investigate incidents ('which requests to int_evt_brandA timed out in the last hour?'). The time range must be ≤ 31 days; default to the last hour if the user gives none. Requires HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN.
safety: Read-only; registered only when HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN is set.
Returns no payload bodies (summary rows only); use the console for bodies. Never calls unsealRequest.

tools.name: hub_admin_request_timeline
tools.title: Request audit timeline (admin, read-only)
tools.description: Operator tool: get the full audit timeline of one request — received, validated, resolved (which integration version, vendor, account and transformers were used), transformed, each upstream attempt and response, and the final outcome — plus the attempt list. Payloads follow the integration's audit policy: masked values are hashes, sealed payloads are null (this tool cannot unseal). Use it to explain why a specific request failed. Requires HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN.

include_payloads.description: Include (masked) event payloads; default returns metadata, sha256 and sizes only to save context.

safety: Read-only; registered only when HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN is set.
Never unseals. Masked/sealed policy is enforced by the Hub, not by hubmcp.

tools.name: hub_admin_breaker_states
tools.title: Circuit breaker states (admin, read-only)
tools.description: Operator tool: list circuit breakers per (account, endpoint) with state (closed / open / half_open), whether an operator forced it, failure ratio, when it reopens, and how many requests are parked behind it. Use it to answer 'is vendor X down?' or 'why are requests queued?'. Filter by vendor_id, account_id or state. Requires HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN.
safety: Read-only; registered only when HUB_ADMIN_TOKEN is set.
Never calls force-open / force-close / clear-force.
